Re: Internal Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Skyler Foster  
Member ID: W718345521  
Reference number: POC-BDD7B46260-11524  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial notice: August 22, 2026  

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing Tufts Health Plan’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lower-back disc surgery/decompression. The stated reason for denial was that the submitted imaging findings did not support medical necessity.

The clinical and imaging records directly demonstrate a structural cause of my persistent, function-limiting neurologic symptoms:

- The June 15, 2026 lumbar MRI shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain extending into the right calf.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- Symptoms have progressively continued for 18 months and have not been relieved by rest.

The MRI is therefore not an incidental or nonspecific finding. It identifies an L4-L5 disc extrusion and severe stenosis at the same level and side that correspond to the documented L5 radicular symptoms, functional limitation, examination findings, and neurologic deficit. These records provide objective anatomic evidence of nerve-root compression and clinical evidence that the compression is producing significant impairment.

I have also completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate improvement:

- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from May 11, 2026, through July 20, 2026. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, as documented in the physical-therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have progressive pain, right-calf radicular symptoms, inability to stand for more than 10 minutes, and a corresponding neurologic deficit.

The records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a nonsmoker. These facts do not identify a documented clinical contraindication to the requested procedure.

I request that Tufts Health Plan overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030. If the denial is upheld, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the exact medical policy or clinical-review guideline applied to CPT 63030, its policy number and version or effective date, the specific criteria relied upon, and the complete case file and medical records considered in making the decision.

I was unable to verify a publicly available Tufts commercial/ACA policy containing the medical-necessity criteria for CPT 63030, so this appeal does not quote a Tufts policy. Please identify and provide the actual criteria applied to this request so that I can fully address the basis for the determination.

Please also arrange review by an appropriately qualified clinical peer who was not involved in the initial denial. The attached records include the lumbar MRI report, physical-therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical documentation.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the appeal decision and any further appeal or external-review rights.

Sincerely,

Skyler Foster  
Member ID: W718345521
